deep.reconstruction:
The page is the blank reverse of a fan-fold line-printer sheet. The printed side, upside down, is an IBM JES2 job banner: 'GUTS', STC 108, ROOM, 3.44.20 PM 16 AUG 82. That date only bounds when the paper was printed. The mathematical content is a short handwritten list (also upside down relative to the print) and a coloured sketch.

The list reads roughly: 'a) côtés marqués ⇒ a') côtés marqués' (the word 'angles' is struck out and replaced, apparently by 'côtés'); 'b) axes critiques marqués sur les arêtes'; 'c) [struck word: points? poids?] des faces'. A double arrow in the margin links a) and c).

In context, Grothendieck is studying systems of pseudo-lines (X, X_1) on a surface X. The previous and next pages build a cellular / polygonal structure from the 'opérations de transition partielles' of a pseudo-line D. They introduce a graph K whose vertices are claimed to be 4-valent, with an exception at 'points d'arrêt' (stopping points). They also discuss elementary moves ('déplacement élémentaire') of a pseudo-line.

This note appears to list the combinatorial decorations needed to encode that structure on the resulting cell complex:
- (a) markings on sides, replacing an earlier idea of markings on angles;
- (b) 'critical axes' recorded on edges;
- (c) some datum attached to faces.

In modern terms this is a decorated cell complex encoding the local behaviour of a family of pseudo-lines, in the spirit of wiring diagrams or oriented-matroid face lattices.

The sketch shows a long (green) line crossed by two orange X's and one orange transversal stroke, with a faint pencil line nearly parallel to the green one. It plausibly depicts a pseudo-line meeting other pseudo-lines. The right-hand X crosses roughly on the green line, suggesting a triple point or a crossing being moved across the line, i.e. a triangle flip / elementary move. The green and orange strokes are overall struck through, perhaps cancelling the sketch. This reading is speculative.
